chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halbi, from his father, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:
I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was praying, so I counted for him in the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood) sixty glorifications (tasbihat).

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ تَغْلِبَ: A prominent narrator of the Imams
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَةً: A glorification (specifically referring to the Tasbih of Fatimah or general tasbih)

ai.seo_question: How many glorifications did the Prophet's family recite during the bowing and prostration of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the specific practice of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reciting sixty glorifications during the bowing and prostration, serving as a primary textual basis for the recommended (mustahabb) quantity of Tasbih in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the importance of mindful devotion (khushu) in prayer, linking physical acts of worship with spiritual remembrance.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ahmad Bin Umar Al Halby, from his father, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,
‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and heasws was praying Salāt. So I numbered for himasws saying during the Rukū and the Sajdah, sixty Glorifications’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from ibn Faddal from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar al-Halabiy from his father from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “
I once went to visit abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when he performed Salah (prayer). I counted his Tasbih in Ruku’ (bowing down on one’s knees) and Sujud (prostration) which were sixty Tasbih.’”
